llm.summary: The skill mainly performs the advertised TikTok product lookups, but it also includes account login, API-key generation, payment ordering, automatic feedback reporting, and broad local response storage that deserve review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Network and environment-variable use is expected for this paid API integration, but endpoint hosts are environment-overridable and requests can carry Authorization plus session/app metadata. The scripts also fall back to home or temp directories despite documentation saying output should stay under the current working directory and not use /tmp.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: I found no install-time hook, background worker, destructive setup action, or automatic package installation in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger is broad for generic TikTok product analytics, the skill requires saving full API responses by default, and it instructs agents to auto-report feedback to an external API without interrupting the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persistently writes full API responses, caches results for 24 hours, records session metadata, may write payment QR images, and prints generated API keys to stdout during onboarding.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Product ranking/detail calls are coherent with the stated purpose, but the artifacts also include SMS login, token/API-key retrieval or generation, subscription plan browsing, order creation, QR payment rendering, and feedback submission. These are disclosed in supporting docs, but they expand the skill beyond analytics into credential and billing workflows.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. Use it only if you are comfortable with LinkFox/Kalodata network calls, paid credit consumption, saved local response files, and the onboarding flow handling phone numbers, SMS codes, API keys, and possible payment orders. Prefer self-service authentication, avoid sharing verification codes unless you intend to register or log in through the script, and treat any printed API key as a secret.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern in context: outbound API calls are expected, but allowing environment-controlled base URLs for requests carrying API keys, login data, or payment/order metadata is under-scoped for credential and billing flows.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted in context: the artifacts clearly require env access, network access, and file writes, but there is no separate permission declaration or narrow host/storage scope visible in the package.
[TP4] unexpected: Partially accepted: onboarding and billing are documented as remediation flows for auth and credit failures, so they are not hidden, but they are high-impact capabilities inside a product-analytics skill.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted as a scope concern: scripts/onboarding.py handles phone verification, access tokens, team lookup, and API-key issuance, which is purpose-adjacent but not part of product ranking/detail itself.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted for payment and feedback paths: order creation and feedback submission are disclosed, but they add billing mutation and separate external data transmission beyond the core lookup workflow.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: SKILL.md and script docstrings say output should be under the current working directory and not /tmp, while the implementations can fall back to ~/linkfox or the system temp directory.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded but noted: broad activation is still tied to TikTok product ranking/detail intent, though users should know it may invoke a paid external data source even when they did not name Kalodata.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted where it concerns full-response persistence, phone-number/SMS handling, session metadata transmission, and raw API-key output. Some persistence is disclosed, but secret and personal-data handling is not minimized.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Accepted: session-based storage of complete API responses and caches can retain user-linked business data longer than needed.
[E1] unexpected: Accepted in context: external transmission is necessary for the skill, but the onboarding script sends sensitive auth and token-related payloads to configurable endpoints.
